gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Synology's own Container Manager (Docker) release notes added the DS223 in version 20.10.23-1405 (2023-05-22), even though ChatGPT's comparison tables mark the DS223 and DS223j as 'Docker: No'. None of them states that Synology's 14.6 dB(A) noise rating for the DS223 was measured with SATA SSDs, not hard drives.
standout_why: Compared against computingforgeeks.com/best-2-bay-nas (cited twice), starryhope.com/nas/best-2-bay-nas (cited), nas.kuibu.net/best/2-bay (cited) and the uncited PCWorld DS223j review. ComputingForGeeks lists the maker noise ratings (18.2 dB(A) for the DS223j) and says the conditions are 'not stated'. It says nothing about Docker for Synology. StarryHope and Kuibu have no noise or Docker data for the DS223 or DS223j. PCWorld, ranked 3 in one chat but never cited, lists 'Docker support' as a DS223j pro, so the DS223j half is partly covered. The DS223 release-note entry and its SSD-only noise test are on none of these pages. Synology's DS223j spec page, which was in the results, does give the DS223j noise test drives.
decides: The Docker finding corrects ChatGPT's tables for the Synology picks. The DS223 has Synology's official Container Manager package, and a named reviewer (PCWorld) lists Docker support on the DS223j, so 'Docker = TerraMaster or UGREEN only' is wrong. Home users who want one or two containers alongside Synology Photos and backups can stay with Synology. The 1 GB and 2 GB of RAM and the ARM chip still limit them to light containers. The noise footnote changes the 'quiet' ranking. Synology's 14.6 dB(A) (DS223, SSDs, idle) and 18.2 dB(A) (DS223j, 2 TB Seagate drives, idle) cannot be compared with UGREEN's 29–34 dB quiet-mode rating or TerraMaster's unconditioned 19 dB(A). The low Synology numbers should not decide a bedroom pick. The TerraMaster F2-425 at $269.99 on the TerraMaster store stays the value pick for Docker and Plex. The UGREEN DXP2800 is $389.99 at UGREEN's own store today, over the budget unless the $296.99 Walmart listing holds.

findings.label: Docker (Container Manager) on stock DSM
findings.value: Officially supported: 'Added support for the following models with the ARMv8 architecture: DS420j, DS223' in Container Manager 20.10.23-1405, published 2023-05-22
findings.source_title: Synology Release Notes for Container Manager
findings.note: This is Synology's own release-notes feed for the package that runs Docker containers in DSM. Version 20.10.23-1437 (2023-09-19) added the DS220j and DS120j. The DS223j is not named in any entry, which fits it launching in June 2023, after 1405. It is a stock package from Package Center with no script needed.

findings.label: Docker (Container Manager)
findings.value: 'Docker support' listed as a pro; PCWorld calls Container Manager 'one of the most important' apps on it
findings.source_title: Synology DiskStation DS223j review: New NAS, same appealing story | PCWorld
findings.note: This is a named reviewer's statement. I couldn't confirm the DS223j on Synology's own applied-model list, which loads dynamically. It uses the same Realtek RTD1619B ARMv8 chip as the DS223, which is officially supported. With 1 GB of RAM, plan on light containers only.

findings.label: Maker noise rating and test condition
findings.value: 14.6 dB(A), 'conducted with the Synology system fully installed with Synology SATA SSDs and in an idle state'
findings.note: This figure is measured with no spinning hard drives, so it cannot be compared with HDD-loaded ratings. Same page: 17.343 W access, 4.08 W HDD hibernation, 2 GB DDR4, 1× 1GbE, 2-year warranty extendable to 4.

findings.label: Maker noise rating and test condition
findings.value: 18.2 dB(A), 'fully loaded with Seagate 2TB ST2000VN000 hard drive(s) in the idle state'; background 16.49–17.51 dB(A)
findings.note: The rating comes from small 2 TB drives at idle in a room already at about 17 dB(A), roughly 1 dB below the rating. Same page: 16.31 W access, 4 W HDD hibernation, 1 GB DDR4, 1× 1GbE with MTU capped at 1500, 2-year warranty extendable to 4.

findings.label: Maker power and noise ratings use different test conditions (as reported by ComputingForGeeks)
findings.value: TerraMaster F2-425 rated 22 W working / 11 W hibernation; UGREEN DXP2800 rated 16.38 W access / 5.24 W hibernation and 29–34 dB in quiet mode; Synology DS223j 16.31 W / 4.00 W
findings.source_title: Best 2-Bay NAS (2026): Backups, Plex, Beginners | ComputingForGeeks
findings.note: ComputingForGeeks says these are maker ratings and that it does not know how the makers tested. It also measured nothing on these units except through cited reviews (ocinside measured the DXP2800 at about 7 W idle and 34.7 W peak). The UGREEN dB range is quiet-mode only. Synology's is HDD idle (DS223j) or SSD idle (DS223), and TerraMaster's has no condition. ComputingForGeeks also reports that installing another OS voids the TerraMaster F2-425's 2-year warranty.
